documents.unit: Office of the Provost and Executive VP for Academic Affairs
documents.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Academic Contexts
documents.summary: Provost-issued university policy (aligned with BOR Policy 6.28) covering AI in teaching, research and administration. It gives faculty academic freedom to use, forbid or structure AI in their courses, requires each syllabus to carry an AI statement, and sets data, tool-vetting, training and governance rules. It treats unauthorized AI-generated submissions as plagiarism and agentic completion of assessments as cheating.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no university-wide rule on student AI use. It says "faculty are free to use, not use, or otherwise structure the use of AI within their courses as they see fit" and requires a syllabus statement sorting uses into "forbidden, restricted, and permitted". The decision is handed to instructors, so delegates, although a Flexible AI Statement Builder is offered as a template.

units.why: The purpose sentence sets the policy aim: "responsible, ethical, and transparent use" across teaching, research and administration. It is an institution-wide framework or preamble (P56), not a rule on one use.
units.anchor: responsible, ethical, and transparent use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools

units.why: "This policy ensures that the University complies with Board of Regents (BOR) Policy 6.28" ties the policy to a system framework and to law. It states institutional purpose and scope, so P56.
units.anchor: complies with Board of Regents (BOR) Policy 6.28 Artificial Intelligence in Academic Context

units.why: "All students, faculty, and staff must be aware of and comply with this policy" binds the whole community and sets scope, so a framework statement (P56).
units.anchor: All students, faculty, and staff must be aware of and comply with this policy

units.why: Users "should be familiar with and comply with" a list of related policies (Academic Dishonesty, Code of Student Conduct, FERPA and others). It situates AI use within existing rules, which fits P56 as scope better than P45 because no collaborator analogy is drawn.
units.anchor: should be familiar with and comply with the Georgia Southern University
units.policy: All students, faculty, and staff should be familiar with and comply with the University and USG policies that govern the use of AI, including the Academic Dishonesty Policy, the Code of Student Conduct, FERPA and the USG Artificial Intelligence Guidelines.

units.why: "recognizes the importance of critically and responsibly integrating appropriate AI technologies to strengthen teaching" is a welcoming institutional position on AI. P02 chosen over P56 because it takes a positive position on use, not only scope.
units.anchor: critically and responsibly integrating appropriate AI technologies to strengthen teaching

units.why: "Research in the field of, and involving the use of AI, is encouraged" welcomes AI in research and requires faculty to follow discipline, funder and publisher rules. It governs scholarship, so P62.
units.anchor: faculty must adhere to the requirements of their disciplines, funding agencies, and publishers
units.policy: Research involving the use of AI is encouraged, and faculty must adhere to the requirements of their disciplines, funding agencies and publishers regarding the use of AI in research, writing or peer review.

units.why: "The University maintains an inventory of permitted AI tools when using institutional and/or student data" means sanctioned tools exist for protected data. P50 (vetted tools) chosen over P17 because this is an institutional inventory driven by data protection, not a course tool.
units.anchor: maintains an inventory of permitted AI tools

units.why: "Only publicly available data may be entered/used in public AI tools" limits what may go into non-inventory tools. It protects data, so P50.
units.anchor: Only publicly available data may be entered/used in public AI tools

units.why: "must not be entered or used in public AI tools" is a flat ban on restricted data going into public tools; P50 (data protection) is the best fit.
units.anchor: must not be entered or used in public AI tools

units.why: "required yearly training for all faculty, staff, and students" is an institutional requirement for training on risks and ethical use. P63 (support in learning AI) is the nearest type; no type covers mandatory training exactly.
units.anchor: required yearly training for all faculty, staff, and students

units.why: The Committee "reviews and implements this policy across the University and makes recommendations on policy updates"; policy governance and revision (P54).
units.anchor: AI Academic Governance Committee, which reviews and implements this policy

units.why: Concerns "should be addressed using existing processes" in the Faculty Handbook and Student Code of Conduct, so suspected misuse is handled as an ordinary integrity matter (P36).
units.anchor: addressed using existing processes that apply to the situation

units.why: "There are no exclusions or exceptions to this policy" sets scope: every member and context is covered, so P56.
units.anchor: There are no exclusions or exceptions to this policy

units.why: The accountability definition says members "are responsible for the content of their work, even if aspects of it are generated by AI", which is ownership of what is submitted (P29).
units.anchor: responsible for the content of their work, even if aspects of it are generated

units.why: The agentive AI definition ("can act independently to achieve goals ... minimal human oversight") sets what the policy covers. P61 rather than P07 because it imposes no rule.
units.anchor: Agentive AI: A type of generative AI in which the system can act independently

units.why: The Committee is "charged with reviewing this policy at least yearly", a review cycle and monitoring duty (P54).
units.anchor: charged with reviewing this policy at least yearly

units.why: "Committee members will review the standard language in the Flexible AI Statement Builder regularly" is a review cycle for the statement language (P54).
units.anchor: review the standard language in the Flexible AI Statement Builder regularly

units.why: "The provost shall appoint the Committee members" and the membership list say who maintains the policy; governance (P54).
units.anchor: The provost shall appoint the Committee members
units.policy: The provost appoints the AI Academic Governance Committee, made up of at least two faculty selected by the Faculty Senate and representatives of the Provost's office, ITS, Legal Affairs, the Library, Research, the Registrar, Human Resources and Student Affairs.

units.why: The definition of AI-generated content ("created by AI models instead of humans") fixes what the policy covers (P61).
units.anchor: created by AI models instead of humans

units.why: "outputs that may favor or discriminate against certain groups" names bias as a harm of generative AI. P53 fits better than P61 because it is a concern, not a scope definition.
units.anchor: outputs that may favor or discriminate against certain groups or concepts

units.why: The AI definition ("technology that enables computer systems to perform complex tasks normally done by humans") sets what counts as AI for the policy, P61.
units.anchor: technology that enables computer systems to perform complex tasks normally done by humans

units.why: The confirmation-bias definition warns users "selectively accept outputs that align with their preexisting beliefs", a named risk of AI use (P53).
units.anchor: selectively accept outputs that align with their preexisting beliefs

units.why: Compliance Recordkeeping says the Office of Institutional Research and Effectiveness "will maintain records of compliance". Keeping records of AI approvals and audits is governance (P54), not P55, which concerns learning effects.
units.anchor: will maintain records of compliance and documentation

units.why: The hallucination definition says AI output may be "plausible sounding but is incorrect, nonsensical, or fabricated", warning that output can be wrong (P31).
units.anchor: plausible sounding but is incorrect, nonsensical, or fabricated

units.why: The Builder "allows faculty to select the language that reflects their decisions" and Legal approved each option. It is a template for instructors who set their own rule (P04); P09 does not fit as it describes a tool, not a requirement.
units.anchor: allows faculty to select the language that reflects their decisions

units.why: "Use of the Flexible AI Statement Builder will provide consistent language for students, which promotes understanding of their responsibilities" explains the communication benefit of shared statements (P09).
units.anchor: consistent language for students, which promotes understanding of their responsibilities

units.why: The generative AI definition ("creates added content, such as text, images, audio, video, and code") sets scope (P61).
units.anchor: Generative AI is a subset of AI that creates added content

units.why: The human-oversight definition describes "mechanisms and processes by which humans monitor, review, and potentially intervene" in AI, a definition (P61).
units.anchor: mechanisms and processes by which humans monitor, review, and potentially intervene

units.why: Process Tracking Software ("Turnitin Clarity, Grammarly Authorship, Visible AI, Codio, CodeGrade") is defined as a platform "to demonstrate the process of developing papers, writing code". Process-evidence tools for showing or checking work, P40.
units.anchor: Turnitin Clarity, Grammarly Authorship, Visible AI, Codio, CodeGrade

units.why: The prompt definition ("Any input, such as a question, command, statement, code ...") defines a term (P61).
units.anchor: Any input, such as a question, command, statement, code, instruction

units.why: "AI tools not included in the University's inventory of permitted AI tools" defines public AI tools, which the data rules depend on (P61).
units.anchor: AI tools not included in the University's inventory of permitted AI tools

units.why: The syllabus statement definition ("Information provided to students outlining specific requirements and expectations") defines the term used by the syllabus rules (P61).
units.anchor: outlining specific requirements and expectations for a course or program

units.why: Transparency defined as "traceability and explainability" and making humans "aware that they are communicating or interacting with an AI system" is a principle definition (P61).
units.anchor: allows appropriate traceability and explainability

units.why: The CIO "shall establish a mechanism for procurement, review, and inventory of all AI tools", setting up the vetting system; P65 (review of AI vendor agreements).
units.anchor: establish a mechanism for procurement, review, and inventory of all AI tools

units.why: The review must "ensure all AI tools (regardless of cost incurred) contain provisions for addressing ethical considerations and include safeguards against bias, hallucinations, and prompt injections", a vendor review criterion (P65).
units.anchor: safeguards against bias, hallucinations, and prompt injections

units.why: AI tools "must be documented in an institutional inventory" with listed data elements. This is an institutional AI inventory, P65 rather than P50 because it addresses the institution, not user behavior.
units.anchor: must be documented in an institutional inventory
units.policy: All AI tools used in the University's environment must be documented in an institutional inventory recording tool name, vendor, tool type, model type, data interaction, data storage and purpose.

units.why: "will be published and made available to the University community" makes the approved list visible, directing users to vetted tools (P50).
units.anchor: published and made available to the University community

units.why: Users "must complete the Third Party Risk Review ... before purchase and/or use of the tool", a required approval step before using a tool (P65).
units.anchor: must complete the Third Party Risk Review for risk assessment and approval

units.why: "All tools shall be reviewed at least annually" is a recurring tool review, closest to P65 (vendor review) rather than P54 (review of the policy).
units.anchor: All tools shall be reviewed at least annually

units.why: "faculty are free to use, not use, or otherwise structure the use of AI within their courses as they see fit" hands the decision to instructors (P04). Neutral because the university itself permits any course stance.
units.anchor: free to use, not use, or otherwise structure the use of AI

units.why: "University faculty have academic freedom to conduct the instruction of their courses and to design their assessments" is the basis for per-instructor rules (P04).
units.anchor: academic freedom to conduct the instruction of their courses and to design their assessments

units.why: "Faculty expectations should be communicated in clear, consistent language in an enforceable syllabus statement" tells faculty to communicate in the syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: communicated in clear, consistent language in an enforceable syllabus statement

units.why: "each faculty member must create an AI syllabus statement" makes a syllabus statement mandatory (P09).
units.anchor: each faculty member must create an AI syllabus statement

units.why: The statement must provide "a working definition of AI as it relates to the course context". It is a definition requirement inside the syllabus; P61 over P09 because the item is about defining scope.
units.anchor: working definition of AI as it relates to the course context and policy

units.why: The statement must give "specific guidance to students about forbidden, restricted, and permitted AI uses for diverse types of course activities". P05 (named categories of use) over P09 because it asks for uses sorted into categories.
units.anchor: forbidden, restricted, and permitted AI uses for diverse types of course activities

units.why: The statement "Outlines scholastic expectations for transparency, including citations of how and to what level AI was incorporated", so it must say how AI use is cited (P24).
units.anchor: citations of how and to what level AI was incorporated

units.why: The statement "communicates the possible use of tools to address unethical usage of AI, including language detection tools, proctoring tools, process analytic tools", so students are told of detection; P40.
units.anchor: possible use of tools to address unethical usage of AI

units.why: "Establishes any requirements for using process tracking software" lets faculty require students to show process; P35 (redesign assessment around AI) over P40 because it is a student-facing requirement tied to assessment.
units.anchor: requirements for using process tracking software
units.policy: The syllabus statement establishes any requirements for using process tracking software.

units.why: "Identifies potential consequences for violation of these policies" requires the statement to say what penalties may follow (P37).
units.anchor: Identifies potential consequences for violation of these policies

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to use the Flexible AI Statement Builder tool" recommends the shared template for syllabus statements (P09).
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to use the Flexible AI Statement Builder tool

units.why: "Using consistent language across multiple courses and/or disciplines clarifies the expectations of each course" gives the reason for shared language (P09).
units.anchor: Using consistent language across multiple courses and/or disciplines clarifies the expectations

units.why: "Faculty should use AI tools that have been licensed by the University" is a faculty rule to use vetted tools for student data; P50 rather than P59 because it concerns data protection, not the teaching task.
units.anchor: Faculty should use AI tools that have been licensed by the University

units.why: "Faculty must ensure compliance with FERPA in the handling of student work, intellectual property, and student data" is a privacy duty when faculty use AI (P50).
units.anchor: Faculty must ensure compliance with FERPA

units.why: "Only University-approved AI tools may be used for assessing student work" limits faculty AI use in assessing. P59 (instructor use of AI in teaching work) chosen because it is about evaluation work; P46 does not apply as grades are not at issue.
units.anchor: Only University-approved AI tools may be used for assessing student work

units.why: "Faculty should inform students of their use of AI for this purpose" is disclosure of instructor AI use (P47).
units.anchor: Faculty should inform students of their use of AI

units.why: "Students are accountable for their use of AI as detailed in the University's Academic Dishonesty Policy" places AI misuse under existing integrity rules (P36).
units.anchor: Students are accountable for their use of AI

units.why: "Any use of AI to generate content that is submitted as one's work without faculty permission and/or proper attribution is considered plagiarism" restricts unpermitted or unattributed AI-generated submissions. P36 (misconduct classification) over P19 because it names a violation and does not ban AI outright.
units.anchor: without faculty permission and/or proper attribution is considered plagiarism

units.why: "Use of agentive AI to complete assessments without human interaction is considered cheating" classes autonomous-agent completion of assessments as cheating. P07 (agents) over P36 because the specific subject is agentic AI.
units.anchor: Use of agentive AI to complete assessments without human interaction is considered cheating

units.why: "Complete the required AI training provided by the University" is a student training duty (P63, the only training type).
units.anchor: Complete the required AI training provided by the University

units.why: "Follow AI guidelines specified in each course" tells students that each course's rule governs them (P11).
units.anchor: Follow AI guidelines specified in each course
units.policy: Students must follow the AI guidelines specified in each course.

units.why: "request clarification if they are uncertain about any policies as established in the syllabus" is the ask-when-unsure rule (P10).
units.anchor: request clarification if they are uncertain about any policies

units.why: "Maintain understanding of university-wide policies regarding the use of AI" asks students to know the institutional rules; P56 as a scope-awareness duty.
units.anchor: Maintain understanding of university-wide policies regarding the use of AI

units.why: "Follow faculty guidance on disclosure and citation of AI assistance in their courses" sets student disclosure as per faculty guidance (P24).
units.anchor: Follow faculty guidance on disclosure and citation of AI assistance

units.why: "Practice human verification and critical evaluation of AI-generated content" requires checking AI output (P31).
units.anchor: Practice human verification and critical evaluation of AI-generated content

units.why: "students remain fully responsible for all submitted work, regardless of the level of AI assistance" is student ownership of submissions (P29).
units.anchor: students remain fully responsible for all submitted work

units.why: "over-reliance on AI may undermine learning objectives and the development of critical thinking skills" gives the learning rationale (P41).
units.anchor: over-reliance on AI may undermine learning objectives

units.why: "maintaining and supporting academic integrity in all coursework, including the use of AI" is a general integrity duty. No type fits exactly; P29 (submit work that is your own) is closest.
units.anchor: maintaining and supporting academic integrity in all coursework, including the use of AI

units.why: "Employees should use AI tools that have been licensed by the University" is a staff rule to use vetted tools (P50).
units.anchor: Employees should use AI tools that have been licensed by the University

units.why: "Student and University-specific information must not be entered or used in public AI tools" is a data ban for staff (P50).
units.anchor: must not be entered or used in public AI tools

units.why: "Users must use only authorized and anonymized data to train or interact with public AI systems" limits data given to public AI (P50).
units.anchor: only authorized and anonymized data to train or interact with public AI systems

units.why: "All AI-generated content must be reviewed by an employee before using it" requires human checking of output (P31).
units.anchor: All AI-generated content must be reviewed by an employee before using it

units.why: "that information may not be used for work purposes" when no reliable source verifies AI output bars unverified output (P31).
units.anchor: that information may not be used for work purposes

units.why: "Staff must complete training in the ethical use of AI in the workplace" is a staff training duty (P63).
units.anchor: Staff must complete training in the ethical use of AI in the workplace

units.why: "this policy and all updates to this policy shall be communicated to all campus stakeholders promptly" is governance of policy communication (P54).
units.anchor: all updates to this policy shall be communicated to all campus stakeholders promptly

units.why: "The University requires training to ensure faculty, staff, and students are well-equipped to engage with AI in a responsible, ethical, and informed manner" requires training for all (P63).
units.anchor: The University requires training to ensure faculty, staff, and students are well-equipped

units.why: "AI tools procured and utilized by stakeholders must adhere to the following principles" opens the ethical-use principles, a framework (P56).
units.anchor: must adhere to the following principles and effective safeguards

units.why: "AI tools must be evaluated for potential biases in their design, training data, and outputs" is a bias principle (P53).
units.anchor: AI tools must be evaluated for potential biases

units.why: "Vendors must provide transparent documentation of how their tools function" sets vendor accountability expectations (P65).
units.anchor: Vendors must provide transparent documentation of how their tools function

units.why: AI applications known to hallucinate "will undergo additional scrutiny or may be disallowed", a tool-review criterion on reliability (P65).
units.anchor: will undergo additional scrutiny or may be disallowed

units.why: "AI should support, not replace, human judgment" says AI must not replace human thinking (P32).
units.anchor: AI should support, not replace, human judgment

units.anchor: AI tools must be accessible to all users, including those with disabilities

units.anchor: susceptibility to prompt injection attacks or malicious manipulation

units.anchor: feeding data into unsecured public AI models is potentially the same

units.anchor: should only be provided to AI models that are listed in the approved inventory

units.anchor: Academic Affairs will lead professional development opportunities for faculty and staff

units.anchor: educational programs designed to build their understanding of AI tools

documents.title: Academic Affairs Policies record 51 (abstract page)
documents.summary: Repository abstract page for the university AI policy. It repeats only the purpose statement of the full policy and adds no new rules.
documents.stance_why: The page states only a purpose ("responsible, ethical, and transparent use") and sets no stance on student AI use itself. The full policy it points to delegates to faculty, so delegates.

units.why: The abstract states the policy aim: "responsible, ethical, and transparent use" of AI across teaching, research and administration, "encouraging innovation, academic freedom, and appropriate autonomy". It is an institution-wide framework or preamble (P56). It repeats the other document but is coded on its own.
units.anchor: responsible, ethical, and transparent use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools

notes: Only a university-layer policy was found. The second document is a repository abstract repeating the purpose sentence. Topic codes come from tools/AGENT_BRIEF.md (CODEBOOK.md refers to it). Judgment calls: the student plagiarism sentence is typed P36 not P19 because the policy does not ban AI outright; training duties typed P63 as the nearest type; vendor and tool-review rules typed P65 though that type's source was Howard. The source has a typo 'Al AI tools' that an anchor-free fragment avoids.
